subject.title: fix(openclaw): prevent private state races during publication

question: Should Crabline adopt this identity-bound private-file mutation-claim design, including its stricter treatment of existing parents, ACLs, owners, and stale claims?
rationale: Tests cannot decide whether the new fail-closed compatibility behavior and cross-platform trust model are the intended permanent security contract.

options.title: Approve after native proof
options.body: Accept the design after native Windows and Linux runs demonstrate publication, cleanup, stale recovery, and upgrade behavior on real filesystems.

options.title: Narrow the hardening
options.body: Retain the established publication contract and land only the smallest independently proven race and path-substitution fixes.

options.title: Pause the redesign
options.body: Keep the current implementation until the ownership, ACL, and stale-claim contract can be specified and reviewed separately.

recommendation.title: Approve after native proof
recommendation.body: Accept the design after native Windows and Linux runs demonstrate publication, cleanup, stale recovery, and upgrade behavior on real filesystems.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member authored the complete focused hardening series and is the strongest available routing candidate for explaining its invariants and coordinating the security decision.
